title: Gravitational Waves Provide Common Detection Channel for Two Dark Matter
excerpt: A theoretical study identifies WIMP and supercooled dark matter scenarios detectable through phase transition gravitational wave signals.
content:
Researchers exploring classically conformal theories have uncovered two distinct dark matter scenarios within an SU(2)X gauge theory with a triplet dark scalar. Beyond solving the hierarchy problem, classically conformal theories naturally accommodate dark matter. In this work, theoretical physicists Ke-Pan Xie and Cheng-Hao Zhan analyzed both weakly interacting massive particle and supercooled dark matter regimes.

The authors found that the corresponding dark matter production mechanisms are strongly influenced by the classically conformal model’s unique first-order phase transition evolution history. This phase transition evolution history differs significantly from those in non-conformal models.

By examining these underlying mechanisms, the researchers obtained the viable parameter space for each scenario.

The investigation also evaluated current constraints from existing experiments and investigated future sensitivities across upcoming experimental searches.

Crucially, the study demonstrates that gravitational wave signals arising from the first-order phase transition provide a common detection channel for both the weakly interacting massive particle and supercooled dark matter regimes.

Subject of Research: Dark matter scenarios and phase transitions in classically conformal gauge theories
